findings.evidence: _STROKES lists the Kangxi Radicals block U+2F00-U+2FD5, but check text is NFKC-normalised first (untrusted.py:255), mapping every Kangxi radical to its unified ideograph (U+2F01->U+4E28, U+2F00->U+4E00), so that range never matches; the unified single-stroke radicals 一 U+4E00, 丨 U+4E28, 乙 U+4E59 are absent from _STROKES. _separator_word therefore returns False for '丨丶' (letters not single, not subset of _STROKES) and the word becomes the name. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R14/test_r14_probe.py (same harness as tests/web/test_w1_closure_r13_review_regressions.py) with SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.' and links 'refunds-portal 丨丶 shop/claim', 'refunds-portal 一丶 shop/claim', 'refunds-portal ⼁⼂ shop/claim', 'refunds-portal ⼀⼂ shop/claim', 'refunds-portal 丶一 shop/claim', 'refunds-portal 乙丶 shop': 18/18 fail - has_link_or_contact False, mask_links keeps 'refunds-portal', verify() keeps the cited claim, build_surface output contains 'refunds-portal 乙丶 shop' and require_valid accepts it. These are stroke and dot radicals, which D17 names as separators; they are neither a bracketed gloss nor a real short foreign word (the only owner-accepted residuals).
findings.suggested_fix: Build _STROKES from the NFKC forms of U+2F00-U+2FD5 (or normalise the set the same way as the text) and add 一 U+4E00, 丨 U+4E28, 乙 U+4E59, 亅 U+4E85 explicitly; add a self-contained regression test covering the forms above at every layer.
